Your assigned parent, `round1/child1`, is not in TASK.md, so I started from `round3/child0`.

What I found:
- **Fewer atoms cannot do better.** At 108 atoms, random restarts give the same weights to 1e-9. Changing the ladder span, the tie offset or the scale split does not help.
- **More atoms is the only gain**, but each atom costs time. Float values for the same structure:

| Atoms | Value |
|---|---|
| 128 | 0.399495 |
| 160 | 0.399734 |
| 256 | 0.400081 |

  Even 256 atoms stays below 0.400695.
- **Certification time sets the cap.** No two partial sums are equal, so the certifier builds a dictionary of about K⁴/6 entries. On this machine:

| Atoms | Certification CPU time |
|---|---|
| 108 | 17 s |
| 116 | 27 s |
| 128 | 70 s |

  Your lane note says 104 atoms certify in about 1 s. I could not reproduce that here, so I stopped at 112. If the scoring machine is that fast, setting `LADDER_ATOMS` in `strategy.py` to 128 gives about +1.7e-4.

**Risk:** 112 atoms may go over the 20 s certification limit. On this loaded machine it took about 19 s of CPU time and 27 s of wall time.

Extra files I made: `strategy_orig.py`, `parent1.py`, `work/` (experiment scripts) and `best.json`/`check_log.jsonl` (made by `check.py`).
